policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads 'I must needs glory' — an explicit rendering of the impersonal δεῖ. The variant δὴ ('Now') is relegated to the margin by the mapped textual note, 'Some ancient authorities read Now to glory is not expedient', which shows the Revisers knew the RP clause and did not print it.

ASV text has 'though it is not expedient' with no dative of person; RP συμφέρει μοι would require 'it is not expedient for me'. The mapped textual note carries the alternative clause to the margin, confirming the text is the impersonal συμφέρον μέν.
ASV text reads 'but I will come to visions', the adversative δὲ; γὰρ would give 'for I will come'. The mapped textual note assigns the whole RP form of the verse to the margin.
χωρὶς and ἐκτὸς are synonyms; 'apart from the body' renders either, and no note is mapped here.

ASV 'save in my weaknesses' does not settle whether 'my' translates RP's μου or is supplied from the anaphoric article — the same verse-9 clause 'my power is made perfect' renders a base lemma δύναμις that carries no μου, so an unitalicized possessive is not a discriminator here.
ASV 'or heareth from me' supplies no object for the second verb; the relative 'that which' governs both clauses, so the English is silent on the indefinite τι.

ASV text runs 'revelations, that I should not be exalted overmuch' with no connective, and the mapped textual note puts the other reading in the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read revelations—wherefore, that etc.' 'Wherefore' is διὸ, so the printed text is the omission.
Σατανᾶ and Σατᾶν are declensional variants of the same name; 'Satan' renders either.

ASV prints 'that I should not be exalted overmuch' twice, at the head and the close of the verse, so the second ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι stands in the text; the Tregelles omission would leave one clause only.

ASV 'for my power is made perfect in weakness' is the natural English of a bare ἡ δύναμις whose possessor the context supplies, as much as of RP's δύναμίς μου; the unitalicized 'my' does not distinguish.

τελεῖται and τελειοῦται are alternative present passives of the same sense; 'is made perfect' renders either. The one mapped note is an alternative_rendering about 'spread a tabernacle over me' and decides nothing.
ASV 'glory in my weaknesses' leaves open whether 'my' renders μου or the possessive force of the article, exactly as at 12:9's 'my power' where the base lemma has no pronoun.

ASV repeats the preposition in the last member — 'in persecutions, in distresses' — which renders ἐν στενοχωρίαις; the base καὶ στενοχωρίαις would yield 'and in distresses' coordinated under the previous ἐν.
ASV reads 'I am become foolish: ye compelled me' with nothing answering RP's added participle καυχώμενος ('in glorying').
ASV 'by signs and wonders and mighty works' renders an instrumental dative, which is the ordinary English of both the bare dative and ἐν with the dative; the added preposition leaves no trace.
τε καὶ and bare καὶ are both Englished 'and'; 'signs and wonders and mighty works' does not show which the Revisers read.
ἡσσώθητε and ἡττήθητε are orthographic variants of one aorist passive; 'ye were made inferior' renders either.
ASV reads 'Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come', where 'this' answers τοῦτο; the RP omission would give only 'the third time'.
'I will not be a burden to you' requires an English object whether or not ὑμῶν stands in the Greek, the person being fixed by the context; the added genitive is invisible in the rendering.
ASV reads a plain conditional, 'If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?'; RP's εἰ καὶ is concessive and would give 'though I love you', as the KJV has it.
ASV 'If I love you more abundantly' can render either the finite ἀγαπῶ or the circumstantial participle ἀγαπῶν under εἰ, which English regularly resolves into a finite clause.
ASV reads 'Ye think all this time that we are excusing ourselves', and 'all this time' is πάλαι; πάλιν would give 'again'.

κατέναντι θεοῦ and κατενώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ are synonymous, and the article is not rendered in English; 'In the sight of God' fits both. The mapped note is an alternative_rendering about the opening clause.
ASV reads the singular 'strife' beside the plurals 'wraths, factions, backbitings', showing number was rendered deliberately; ἔρεις would be 'strifes'.
ASV reads the singular 'jealousy' in a list whose plurals ('wraths', 'factions') are kept plural; RP's ζῆλοι would be 'jealousies'.
The genitive absolute ἐλθόντος μου and the accusative ἐλθόντα με both yield ASV's 'when I come'; English temporal subordination hides the construction.
ASV 'lest ... my God should humble me' renders μὴ with either the aorist subjunctive or the future indicative, both of which English carries with 'should'.
ASV 'should humble me' supplies an object the RP reading already carries in its accusative ἐλθόντα με; the English shows one 'me' either way.
